_comment: Dialogue graphs for the Lakkahaltia case. Portable: each node is plain data a tabletop GM can read aloud. Conditions/effects are evaluated by src/godot/case_state.gd; there is no prose in code.

d1.speaker: Dr. Aino Kivi
d1.text: You are early. The ward does not open until nine, and the ward is not open at all. Which is it, Inspector?

choices.text: "UNSA received a call from this address."

effects.journal: Kivi recognized the patient number before I said it.

d2.speaker: Dr. Aino Kivi
d2.text: The line was disconnected in March. I signed the order myself. If someone called you, they called from a room that has no telephone.

d3.speaker: Dr. Aino Kivi
d3.text: Sixteen was discharged in March with the others. She came back in June. I did not ask how. The paperwork for her return is in the record — one file, two admissions. I have stopped trying to make it consistent.

effects.journal: Kivi is not lying. She is afraid of the paperwork.

d4.speaker: Dr. Aino Kivi
d4.text: The roster runs to June. I signed it every week until June. I remember signing it in a room that smelled of cloudberry, which is not a thing that grows in Helsinki.

choices.text: "Or a memory that does not fit the building."

d5.speaker: Dr. Aino Kivi
d5.text: Read whatever you like. Talk to Salmi before you go — he was on nights in June. And Inspector: do not look into the mirror in sixteen. The patients asked me to take it down. I did not.

n1.speaker: Nurse Väinö Salmi
n1.text: Visitors sign in. Nobody signed in. That is the whole of what I know, and I have said it four times to four different people who all wrote it down differently.

n2.speaker: Nurse Väinö Salmi
n2.text: Two from the city, one from the university, one who did not give a name and smelled of cloudberry. The last one sat with sixteen all night. In the morning there was a second admission in the book and no visitor.

choices.text: "You let a stranger sit with a patient?"

n3.speaker: Nurse Väinö Salmi
n3.text: March. The order says March. But I worked nights until June, and so did the roster, and so did the light in the corridor. You tell me which of those is the record and which is the ward.

choices.text: "The ward you worked is the record."

n4.speaker: Nurse Väinö Salmi
n4.text: Small. Polite. Wore a coat that was too warm for June. Asked whether we had cloudberry jam in the kitchen. Sixteen says it asked her the same question. I have not slept properly since.

effects.journal: Salmi's visitor and Patient 16's visitor agree on cloudberries.

p1.speaker: Patient 16
p1.text: You are the one from the mirror. No — you are the one who has not looked yet. Sit down. The chair is real. I have checked.

p2.speaker: Patient 16
p2.text: Eeva, on the days the ward is open. On the other days I am sixteen. The visitor called me by the number and asked for cloudberries, so I think it had read the file and not the person.

choices.text: "That is a delusion. You know that."

p3.speaker: Patient 16
p3.text: Small. Too many eyes for a face, but it was not frightening. It came out of the mirror and went back through it. It left a stain on the sheet. Kivi had the sheet tested. The result was 'no result', which is not the same as nothing.

effects.journal: The sheet was tested. Check what the lab returned.

p4.speaker: Patient 16
p4.text: Yes. I know that. I also know the mirror is still on the wall, and that you will look into it, because everyone does. When you do, remember that it was polite. That is the part nobody writes down.

p5.speaker: Patient 16
p5.text: The door sticks. Push it with your shoulder, not your hand.
